# [STORY] As an operator, I want every ai-service entry point to authenticate its caller and treat interpolated text as data, so identity and prompt boundaries can't be asserted around

## User Story

**As an** operator of LMDB's AI features
**I want** every entry point into ai-service to authenticate its caller correctly and treat interpolated text as data, not instructions
**So that** identity, service-to-service, and prompt boundaries can't be crossed by a caller who simply asserts what they want to be true

## Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then)

- [x] Given a request to a user-scoped ai-service endpoint, when it is processed, then the caller's identity comes only from the gateway-authenticated header, never from the request body
- [x] Given a request with no `Authorization` header, when api-gateway forwards it, then no client-supplied identity header reaches any downstream service
- [x] Given a call to ai-service's gRPC surface, when it does not present the configured service token, then it is rejected before reaching any business logic
- [x] Given text from a caller or from an upstream service, when it is interpolated into a model prompt, then it cannot forge additional conversation turns or role instructions
- [x] Given the offline speech-to-text model is fetched at image build time, when the fetched archive doesn't match the pinned checksum, then the build fails rather than unpacking it
